findings.claim: The progress tracker points the next pending action at a task that was explicitly skipped, so the orchestrator's own next-step guidance contradicts the plan.
findings.evidence: progress.json hunk sets `"next_task_pending": "Add multi-store tests for projections, membership, relationships, preview propagation, successful restore, and conflict refusal."` — that is the text of task 6, which tasks.md now marks `(SKIPPED)`, while the actual open work is task 10 (docs/ledger/evidence sync, IN_PROGRESS).
findings.suggested_fix: Set next_task_pending to the task 10 text (synchronize ledgers, docs, fixtures, evidence receipts, refiner, adversarial review).

findings.claim: Production code was extended outside the optional devtools subpath despite the acceptance criterion restricting the change surface to @prometheus-ags/entity-graph-core/devtools.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion: "Extend only `@prometheus-ags/entity-graph-core/devtools`; normal core root imports remain free of the optional inspection implementation." The diff adds a new exported function `getRegisteredSchemas()` to `src/crud/relations.ts`, which is part of the root CRUD module, not the devtools subpath.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the registry read inside the devtools module (e.g., a devtools-local accessor injected via the existing registry), or document in the change record that this root-level accessor addition is a deliberate, reviewed exception to the criterion.

findings.claim: Entity revision map keys are built by naive string concatenation and can collide across distinct (type, id) pairs, corrupting conflict detection for preview/restore.
findings.evidence: controller.ts hunk: `entityValueRevisions.get(`${type}:${id}`) ?? 0`. A store with type `a:b`, id `c` collides with type `a`, id `b:c` (both keys `a:b:c`). The README itself uses colon-containing identifiers such as viewId `users:active-table` and queryKey `users:active`, so colons in identifiers are an established pattern in this codebase.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the maps with a nested Map<type, Map<id, number>> or a length-prefixed/JSON-encoded composite key (e.g., JSON.stringify([type, id])).

findings.claim: The preview-entity-patch payload parser validates only the patch's shape, not its keys, so transport-supplied patches containing dangerous keys such as __proto__/constructor/prototype are passed straight into the graph patch layer.
findings.evidence: controller.ts hunk `parsePreviewPayload` checks only `typeof candidate.patch === "object"`, non-null, non-array, and `Object.keys(...).length > 0`, then the command handler calls `previewController.apply(payload.type, payload.id, payload.patch)` with the raw object. This is a boundary input arriving over the transport from arbitrary DevTools clients.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject patches whose own keys include __proto__, constructor, or prototype before calling apply, and use Object.create(null) or a fresh object copy when forwarding the patch.

findings.claim: The viewIds field doc comment is stale and now misdescribes shipped behavior.
findings.evidence: protocol.ts hunk: `/** Populated by the view-membership registry in the next inspection layer. */` on `viewIds`, but the same diff wires `viewRegistry.getViewIdsByEntity()` into `getEntityRecords()`, so the membership layer is present, not "next".
findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment to describe current behavior, e.g. "Stable IDs of registered views currently displaying this entity."

findings.claim: Skipped tasks retain unchecked markdown checkboxes, making the task list ambiguous to any parser or reader that keys off checkbox state.
findings.evidence: tasks.md hunk: `- [ ] 6 — Add multi-store tests ... (SKIPPED)`, `- [ ] 7 ... (SKIPPED)`, `- [ ] 8 ... (SKIPPED)` — the `- [ ]` prefix signals pending while the suffix says skipped.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a distinct marker for skipped tasks (e.g., `- [-]` or strike-through) so skipped is distinguishable from pending.

findings.claim: The new JSON subpath export has no documented consumption contract; Node ESM consumers importing it without import attributes will fail at runtime.
findings.evidence: package.json hunk adds `"./devtools/fixtures/entity-inspection-v1.json": { "default": "./fixtures/devtools/entity-inspection-v1.json" }`. Node requires `import ... with { type: "json" }` for JSON modules; neither the README section documenting the fixture (`entity-inspection-v1.json`) nor the export advertises this.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a README snippet showing the import-attribute form (and the readFile fallback) for the fixture subpath.
